name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Tanker hit off Khasab 18 Nov; 7 since 10 Nov
summary: Tanker hit near Khasab on 18 Nov after an LPG carrier was abandoned on 17 Nov; Hormuz attacks run at about one a day
state: UKMTO said a tanker outbound through Hormuz was hit in the engine room about 6nm north of Khasab, Oman, on 18 Nov; all crew were reported safe (Gulf News). The LPG tanker Tara Gas was struck twice on 16–17 Nov and abandoned, with one crew member missing; attacks near the strait average about one a day (New York Times). UKMTO has reported seven attacks in or near Hormuz since 10 Nov (Hellenic Shipping News). Some tanker traffic moves under US escort, but transits remain impeded.
for_you: Ships transiting the Gulf, Hormuz and Red Sea face attack risk; operators should follow UKMTO and JMIC advisories. Delays and higher insurance costs can feed through to freight rates and delivery times for imported goods.
rubric_hit: Alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded by repeated attacks (7 since 10 Nov)

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
